data.claim: A running ddflow imported from a foreign lane's linked worktree crashes once that tree merges, and nothing detects or heals it at runtime
data.falsifier: package_parent() against primary_checkout() flags a synthetic worktree import and repoint_shared_editable rewrites .pth to the primary
data.mechanism: shared .venv .pth repointed at a doomed worktree; isolate_venv only prevents the repoint at create/adopt
data.question: How does a running ddflow come to import from a foreign lane's worktree, and how can it be detected and healed so the CLI never runs another lane's unmerged code?

chunk_findings.detail: A git or cwd failure while identifying the caller is treated as “foreign”, so a legitimate import from the caller’s own linked worktree is refused. `W.current(Path(os.getcwd()))` is wrapped in `except Exception: own = None`, and the only allow-path is `own is not None and own.path.resolve() == foreign.worktree.resolve()`. Given the editable install pointing at the caller’s worktree (the case the comment calls legitimate) and `os.getcwd()` raising `FileNotFoundError` because the cwd was removed, or `W.current` raising because git cannot be read, `own` stays None, `repoint_shared_editable` runs, and the function returns `FAIL`. That contradicts the same function’s contract that a git or env failure must not block every command (the `foreign_launch_root` failure path returns `OK`).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/cli.py:_guard_foreign_launch

chunk_findings.detail: The heal that is supposed to stop the next process importing the doomed tree does not update the file that actually controls imports unless the `.pth` text is exactly `str(foreign.resolve())`. `direct_url.json` is matched after `Path(...).resolve()`, but the `.pth` check is `read_text().strip() == str(foreign_resolved)`, and a miss is swallowed. Given a shared editable `.pth` whose line is the path pip recorded, `[REDACTED:path]`, while that path’s `resolve()` is `/private/home/dev/proj/.ddflow/worktrees/lane-a` (symlink prefix, typical on macOS), the URL may be rewritten and `changed` may become True, but the `.pth` is left pointing at `lane-a`. The CLI still prints that the install “was reset” and returns `FAIL`. The re-run adds the same `.pth` line to `sys.path`, imports that lane again, and refuses again, so the ModuleNotFoundError crash is replaced by a permanent lockout until the `.pth` is fixed by hand.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/install_info.py:repoint_shared_editable

chunk_findings.detail: The suite locks in the wrong predicate for B-cli-ran-code-from-another-lanes-worktree. The bug and this file's own docstring say the caller's own linked worktree is a legitimate import root and only another lane's tree is not, but `test_running_from_a_linked_worktree_is_detected_as_foreign` sets `PATHS.package_parent` to the process's own worktree and asserts `foreign_launch_root()` is that tree. `repoint_shared_editable` is only exercised as "anything not the primary must be rewritten to the primary". Given a lane whose cwd and imported tree are both its own worktree (no other lane), this passes only if the CLI treats that launch as foreign and rewrites the shared editable install away from the caller's tree — the failure mode the bug said must remain allowed, and the same shared-venv rewrite the report guessed caused the crash.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_foreign_worktree_import.py:44

chunk_findings.detail: A git or cwd lookup failure is treated as “not the caller’s tree” and still rewrites the shared install. If this process was imported from the caller’s own linked worktree (legitimate) and `W.current(Path(os.getcwd()))` raises, `own` is set to None, the `own.path.resolve() == foreign.worktree.resolve()` check is skipped, and `repoint_shared_editable` runs before `return FAIL`. That retargets the shared editable install away from the caller’s tree and blocks the command, which contradicts the function’s own rule that a git/env failure must not keep commands from running.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/cli.py:_guard_foreign_launch

chunk_findings.detail: The file that actually puts the foreign tree on `sys.path` is often left unchanged, while the CLI always claims the install was reset. The `.pth` is updated only when its text equals `str(foreign.resolve())`. The string Python imported from (and that pip wrote) is `str(foreign)` before symlink resolution — e.g. `.pth` contains `/tmp/lane` while `resolve()` is `/private/tmp/lane` — so the write is skipped. `direct_url.json` is matched via `Path.resolve()`, so metadata can move to the primary while the `.pth` still names the doomed worktree. `_guard_foreign_launch` ignores the `False` return and prints that the install was reset; the re-run imports the same foreign tree and is refused again.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/install_info.py:repoint_shared_editable

chunk_findings.detail: The regression locks in the wrong notion of "foreign". The bug text says a launch is bad only when the imported tree is another lane's worktree, and that the caller's own tree is legitimate. `checkout` sets `PATHS.package_parent` to the linked worktree the process is running from, and `test_running_from_a_linked_worktree_is_detected_as_foreign` then requires `foreign_launch_root()` to return that same tree. Given a normal lane launch whose code comes from `.ddflow/worktrees/fix-B-hy-stop-protocol` (the caller), this test demands a foreign hit, so a fix that satisfies it will repoint or abort that run. The case that actually crashed — import root is lane B while the caller is lane A or primary — is never constructed, so the stated failure can still pass these tests.

chunk_findings.detail: `_guard_foreign_launch` catches exceptions when attempting to identify the caller's worktree (`W.current(Path(os.getcwd()))`) and returns `OK`. Given a shell operating inside a deleted or inaccessible foreign worktree directory, line 363 catches the exception and returns `OK`, allowing the foreign worktree's code to execute undetected and risking a crash.

chunk_findings.detail: The heal that is supposed to stop the next process importing the doomed tree does not update the file that actually controls imports unless the `.pth` text is exactly `str(foreign.resolve())`. `direct_url.json` is matched after `Path(...).resolve()`, but the `.pth` check is `read_text().strip() == str(foreign_resolved)`, and a miss is swallowed. Given a shared editable `.pth` whose line is the path pip recorded, `[REDACTED:path]`, while that path’s `resolve()` is `/private/home/dev/proj/.ddflow/worktrees/lane-a` (symlink prefix, typical on macOS), the URL may be rewritten and `changed` may become True, but the `.pth` is left pointing at `lane-a`. The CLI still prints that the install “was reset” and returns `FAIL`. The re-run adds the same `.pth` line to `sys.path`, imports that lane again, and refuses again, so the ModuleNotFoundError crash is replaced by a permanent lockout until the `.pth` is fixed by hand.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/install_info.py:repoint_shared_editable

chunk_findings.detail: The suite locks in the wrong predicate for B-cli-ran-code-from-another-lanes-worktree. The bug and this file's own docstring say the caller's own linked worktree is a legitimate import root and only another lane's tree is not, but `test_running_from_a_linked_worktree_is_detected_as_foreign` sets `PATHS.package_parent` to the process's own worktree and asserts `foreign_launch_root()` is that tree. `repoint_shared_editable` is only exercised as "anything not the primary must be rewritten to the primary". Given a lane whose cwd and imported tree are both its own worktree (no other lane), this passes only if the CLI treats that launch as foreign and rewrites the shared editable install away from the caller's tree — the failure mode the bug said must remain allowed, and the same shared-venv rewrite the report guessed caused the crash.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_foreign_worktree_import.py:44

chunk_findings.detail: `_guard_foreign_launch` catches exceptions when attempting to identify the caller's worktree (`W.current(Path(os.getcwd()))`) and returns `OK`. If a user is running the CLI from within a foreign worktree that has been deleted or has a broken path, `os.getcwd()` or `W.current` raises an exception, which causes the guard to return `OK` instead of detecting the foreign tree and refusing/healing it. Given a shell operating inside a deleted or inaccessible foreign worktree directory, line 363 catches the exception and returns `OK`, allowing the foreign worktree's code to execute undetected and risking a crash.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/cli.py:_guard_foreign_launch

chunk_findings.detail: A failure while identifying the caller is still treated as foreign, so a legitimate import from the caller’s own linked worktree is refused. The new `except Exception` block returns `FAIL` whenever `W.current(Path(os.getcwd()))` raises, and the only allow-path remains `own is not None and own.path.resolve() == foreign.worktree.resolve()`. Given the editable install already pointing at the caller’s worktree (the case the function comment calls legitimate) and `os.getcwd()` raising `FileNotFoundError` because that shell’s cwd was removed, line 363 returns `FAIL` and prints “refusing to run code that may be another lane’s”. The import root is the caller’s own tree, so the command should run; this change does not add any other way to recognise that, and `test_identifying_the_caller_failing_refuses_without_repointing` now requires the false refusal.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/cli.py:_guard_foreign_launch

chunk_findings.detail: The new test does not enforce the “without repointing” half of the contract it names. It patches `I.repoint_shared_editable` to a lambda that returns `True` and only asserts `_guard_foreign_launch() == CLI.FAIL`. If the `except` path also called `repoint_shared_editable(foreign, primary)` before returning `FAIL`, this test would still pass, and the next process would be pinned to the primary even when the import root was the caller’s own tree — the stranding case the new comment says the heal must not do.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_foreign_worktree_import.py:test_identifying_the_caller_failing_refuses_without_repointing

chunk_findings.detail: A git or cwd lookup failure is treated as “not the caller’s tree” and still rewrites the shared install. If this process was imported from the caller’s own linked worktree (legitimate) and `W.current(Path(os.getcwd()))` raises, `own` is set to None, the `own.path.resolve() == foreign.worktree.resolve()` check is skipped, and `repoint_shared_editable` runs before `return FAIL`. That retargets the shared editable install away from the caller’s tree and blocks the command, which contradicts the function’s own rule that a git/env failure must not keep commands from running.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/cli.py:_guard_foreign_launch

chunk_findings.detail: The file that actually puts the foreign tree on `sys.path` is often left unchanged, while the CLI always claims the install was reset. The `.pth` is updated only when its text equals `str(foreign.resolve())`. The string Python imported from (and that pip wrote) is `str(foreign)` before symlink resolution — e.g. `.pth` contains `/tmp/lane` while `resolve()` is `/private/tmp/lane` — so the write is skipped. `direct_url.json` is matched via `Path.resolve()`, so metadata can move to the primary while the `.pth` still names the doomed worktree. `_guard_foreign_launch` ignores the `False` return and prints that the install was reset; the re-run imports the same foreign tree and is refused again.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/install_info.py:repoint_shared_editable

chunk_findings.detail: The regression locks in the wrong notion of "foreign". The bug text says a launch is bad only when the imported tree is another lane's worktree, and that the caller's own tree is legitimate. `checkout` sets `PATHS.package_parent` to the linked worktree the process is running from, and `test_running_from_a_linked_worktree_is_detected_as_foreign` then requires `foreign_launch_root()` to return that same tree. Given a normal lane launch whose code comes from `.ddflow/worktrees/fix-B-hy-stop-protocol` (the caller), this test demands a foreign hit, so a fix that satisfies it will repoint or abort that run. The case that actually crashed — import root is lane B while the caller is lane A or primary — is never constructed, so the stated failure can still pass these tests.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_foreign_worktree_import.py:44

chunk_findings.detail: Lookup failure is now treated as permission to keep running. The guard only reaches `W.current` after a linked-worktree import root is already in hand (`foreign.worktree` on the next line). Given that root is lane A's tree, the caller is in lane B, and `W.current(Path(os.getcwd()))` raises (deleted cwd, git error), the new `return OK` skips both the own-tree check and any heal. The process then executes A's unmerged code — the bug this change is supposed to stop. `test_identifying_the_caller_failing_is_not_a_refusal` locks that in. Failing to identify the caller is not evidence the import is the caller's tree; refuse without repointing.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/cli.py:_guard_foreign_launch

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier wrong contract is untouched: this delta is `+53 -0` and does not edit `foreign_launch_root` or `test_running_from_a_linked_worktree_is_detected_as_foreign`. That test still requires a launch whose code comes from the caller's own linked worktree (`.ddflow/worktrees/fix-B-hy-stop-protocol`) to be reported as foreign. The new CLI tests only stub `_guard_foreign_launch` and do not correct that detector, so any caller that treats a non-None root as foreign still refuses a legitimate own-tree launch.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_foreign_worktree_import.py:44

chunk_findings.detail: The previous contract bug is untouched by this delta. `foreign_launch_root` and `test_running_from_a_linked_worktree_is_detected_as_foreign` are not in the hunks, so a launch whose code comes from the caller’s own linked worktree (`.ddflow/worktrees/fix-B-hy-stop-protocol`, with `PATHS.package_parent` set to that tree) is still required to be reported as foreign. The new CLI tests only stub `_guard_foreign_launch`’s failure path; any caller that treats a non-None root as foreign still refuses a legitimate own-tree run, which is the opposite of the bug’s expected behavior.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_foreign_worktree_import.py:44

chunk_findings.detail: The renamed test claims a lookup failure refuses without retargeting the shared install, but it never checks that. `repoint_shared_editable` is replaced with `lambda foreign, primary: True` and the only assertion is `== CLI.FAIL`. If the guard calls that heal and then returns `FAIL` — the earlier defect on this path — the test still passes.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_foreign_worktree_import.py:test_identifying_the_caller_failing_refuses_without_repointing
